# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.

- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-webpack5';
import React from 'react';

  StoreIcon,
  UserIcon,
  VisaIcon,
} from '.';

const meta: Meta = {
  title: 'Foundation/Icons',
};
export default meta;

type Story = StoryObj;

type IconEntry = { name: string; component: React.ElementType; status: 'custom' | 'base' };

const STATUS_LABEL: Record<IconEntry['status'], string> = {
  custom: 'Custom',
  base: 'Base-mapped',
};

const STATUS_COLOUR: Record<IconEntry['status'], string> = {
  custom: 'green.600',
  base: 'blue.600',
};

function IconGrid({ icons }: { icons: IconEntry[] }) {
  return (
    <SimpleGrid columns={[3, 4, 6, 8]} gap={6}>
      {icons.map(({ name, component: Icon, status }) => (
        <VStack key={name} gap={1} align="center">
          <Box p={2} borderRadius="md" bg="gray.50">
            <Icon boxSize={5} />
          </Box>
          <Text fontSize="10px" textAlign="center" lineHeight="1.2">
            {name}
          </Text>
          <Text fontSize="9px" color={STATUS_COLOUR[status]}>
            {STATUS_LABEL[status]}
          </Text>
        </VStack>
      ))}
    </SimpleGrid>
  );
}

function Section({ title, description, children }: { title: string; description?: string; children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <Box mb={10}>
      <Text fontWeight="bold" fontSize="sm" mb={1}>
        {title}
      </Text>
      {description && (
        <Text fontSize="xs" color="gray.700" mb={4}>
          {description}
        </Text>
      )}
      {children}
    </Box>
  );
}

import React from 'react';
import { iconSizes } from 'app/theme/foundation';
import {
  ArrowDownIcon,
  ArrowLinkIcon,
  ArrowUpIcon,
  BagIcon,
  BagSelectedIcon,
  BagSolidIcon,
  CalendarIcon,
  CarouselIcon,
  CarouselSelectedIcon,
  ChatIcon,

  PauseIcon,
  PlayIcon,
  PlusIcon,
  ProfileIcon,
  SearchIcon,
  ShareIcon,
  ShareTwoIcon,
  WishlistIcon,
  WishlistSolidIcon,
  PhoneIcon,
  WhatsAppIcon,
  EmailIcon,
} from 'app/components/icons';

// Figma iconography spec: node 1892:59595 — 34 of 34 types implemented.
export type ZimmIconType =
  | 'arrow-down'
  | 'arrow-link'
  | 'arrow-up'
  | 'bag'
  | 'bag-selected'
  | 'bag-solid'
  | 'calendar'
  | 'carousel'
  | 'carousel-selected'
  | 'chat'
  | 'check'
  | 'chevron-down'
  | 'chevron-left'
  | 'chevron-right'
  | 'chevron-up'
  | 'close'
  | 'delete'
  | 'edit'
  | 'external-link'
  | 'info'
  | 'info-selected'
  | 'location'
  | 'menu'
  | 'minus'
  | 'mute'
  | 'password'
  | 'pause'
  | 'play'
  | 'plus'
  | 'profile'
  | 'search'
  | 'share'
  | 'share-2'
  | 'wishlist'
  | 'wishlist-solid'
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  | 'phone'
  | 'whatsapp'
  | 'email';

export type ZimmIconSize = keyof typeof iconSizes;

type ZimmIconProps = {
  type: ZimmIconType;
  size?: ZimmIconSize;
  /** Pass Chakra token strings or CSS keywords (e.g. 'text.primary', 'currentColor').
   *  Do not pass hardcoded hex values — use theme tokens. */
  color?: string;
} & ({ 'aria-hidden': true; 'aria-label'?: never } | { 'aria-hidden'?: never; 'aria-label': string });

const ICON_MAP = {
  'arrow-down': ArrowDownIcon,
  'arrow-link': ArrowLinkIcon,
  'arrow-up': ArrowUpIcon,
  bag: BagIcon,
  'bag-selected': BagSelectedIcon,
  'bag-solid': BagSolidIcon,
  calendar: CalendarIcon,
  carousel: CarouselIcon,
  'carousel-selected': CarouselSelectedIcon,
  chat: ChatIcon,
  check: CheckIcon,
  'chevron-down': ChevronDownIcon,
  'chevron-left': ChevronLeftIcon,
  'chevron-right': ChevronRightIcon,
  'chevron-up': ChevronUpIcon,
  close: CloseIcon,
  delete: DeleteIcon,
  edit: EditIcon,
  'external-link': ExternalLinkIcon,
  info: InfoIcon,
  'info-selected': InfoSelectedIcon,
  location: LocationIcon,
  menu: MenuIcon,
  minus: MinusIcon,
  mute: MuteIcon,
  password: PasswordShowIcon,
  pause: PauseIcon,
  play: PlayIcon,
  plus: PlusIcon,
  profile: ProfileIcon,
  search: SearchIcon,
  share: ShareIcon,
  'share-2': ShareTwoIcon,
  wishlist: WishlistIcon,
  'wishlist-solid': WishlistSolidIcon,
  // Footer-specific custom icons — not yet in Figma node 1892:59595,
  // pending addition to the iconography spec in the next design sync.
  phone: PhoneIcon,
  whatsapp: WhatsAppIcon,
  email: EmailIcon,
} as const;

/** Atom — single icon from the Zimmermann icon set. Mirrors zimm-icon contract. */
export const ZimmIcon = ({ type, size = 'md', color = 'currentColor', ...aria }: ZimmIconProps) => {
  const Icon = ICON_MAP[type];
  // Both keys exist in every member of the union (one required, one optional-`never`), so the
  // rest object is indexable directly. The XOR is enforced by ZimmIconProps, not by a cast —
  // casting here only widened 'aria-hidden' from `true | undefined` to `boolean | undefined`.
  const ariaHidden = aria['aria-hidden'];
  const ariaLabel = aria['aria-label'];
  return (
    <Icon
      boxSize={iconSizes[size]}
      color={color}
      aria-hidden={ariaHidden}
      aria-label={ariaLabel}
      role={ariaLabel ? 'img' : undefined}
    />
  );
};

1	import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
5	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
6	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
7	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
8	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
9	 * type/colour.)
10	 *
11	 * Single visual node, no independent per-part state — `defineStyleConfig` + `useStyleConfig(...,
12	 * {variant})` (ZimmNavItem's / ZimmWishlistBadge's pattern) applies directly here, rather than
13	 * ZimmQuantityStepper's function-form `baseStyle` (which exists there because that recipe has
14	 * multiple PARTS needing independent values from one shared boolean, not a single Chakra-native
15	 * `variant` switch).
16	 *
17	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
18	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
19	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
20	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
21	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
22	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
23	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
24	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
25	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
26	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
27	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below to override the textStyle-expanded medium
28	 * value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied after the textStyle expansion
29	 * wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already
30	 * documents and relies on for the identical reason.
31	 *
32	 * `width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly, rather
33	 * than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default.
34	 *
35	 * No low-stock variant: a separate requirement explicitly forbids low-stock messaging at the
36	 * cart level (SFCC-795 §11.2 build decisions) — the variants map below only ever has the two
37	 * keys `error`/`warning`; do not add a third.
38	 */
39	const baseStyle = {
40	  textStyle: 'caption',
41	  fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
42	  width: 'full',
43	};
44	
45	const variants = {
46	  // Figma `text/error` #9c0000 -> status.error (session-notes.md §11.10(6) colour audit).
47	  error: {
48	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)',
49	  },
50	  // Figma `text/muted` / `text/subtlest` #969696 -> both collapse onto this one token, no
51	  // ambiguity in this codebase's own set (session-notes.md §11.10(6)).
52	  //
53	  // Max-quantity messaging ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") uses THIS variant,
54	  // not `error` — even though its own requirement/AC text uses the word "error" to describe it.
55	  // That word is describing "user-facing feedback" in the requirement's own vocabulary, not
56	  // asserting the error SEVERITY tier: the actual Figma design and that story's own AC agree the
57	  // rendered treatment is grey/warning, not red/error. Deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation,
58	  // settled at this build's planning gate — not a mistake, and not to be "corrected" back to
59	  // `error` by a future reader matching the word alone.
60	  warning: {
61	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)',
62	  },
63	};
64	
65	export const ZimmInlineMessage = defineStyleConfig({
66	  baseStyle,
67	  variants,
68	});
69

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	
4	const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';
5	
6	export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
7	  /**
8	   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
9	   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
10	   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
11	   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
12	   */
13	  variant: 'error' | 'warning';
14	  /**
15	   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
16	   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
17	   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
18	   * §11.2 exact copy).
19	   */
20	  text: string;
21	};
22	
23	/**
24	 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
25	 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
26	 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
27	 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
28	 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
29	 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
30	 *
31	 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
32	 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's quantity display
33	 * (zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx's own `<chakra.span __css={styles.value} aria-live="polite">`) —
34	 * so a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
35	 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
36	 *
37	 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
38	 */
39	export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({ variant, text }: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
40	  const styles = useStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });
41	
42	  return (
43	    <chakra.p __css={styles} aria-live="polite" data-testid="zimm-inline-message">
44	      {text}
45	    </chakra.p>
46	  );
47	};

1	import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';
2	import { DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT } from 'app/theme/components/zimmDrawerShared';
3	
4	// Figma's actual named drawer sizes (SFCC-898) — five named sizes, not the three/four this
5	// file previously guessed at. Each name below matches Figma's own naming exactly, so there's
6	// no re-deriving which number belongs to which concept next time this file is touched:
7	//
8	//   Desktop Large — 50%  — Product Details, Filters (desktop width)
9	//   Tablet        — 80%  — Product Details, Filters (tablet width)
10	//   Desktop Small — 25%  — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront,
11	//                           Cookies, Login
12	//   X-Large       — 82%  — Cart. SFCC-11: this is the named-size *library* annotation, not a
13	//                           measurement of the real Cart composition — see `WIDTH_XLARGE` below,
14	//                           which corrects it a second time against the actual frames.
15	//   Mobile        — unchanged, the baseStyle treatment every variant collapses to below `md`.
16	//
17	// An earlier revision of this file measured 82% off a Figma frame annotated "Tablet = 82% of
18	// screen" and used it as `small`'s (now `tablet`'s) value — that frame's annotation was wrong
19	// (or superseded): 82% is actually X-Large's value (Cart), a completely different drawer this
20	// codebase hasn't built yet, and Tablet is genuinely 80%. Corrected once confirmed directly
21	// against the list above, not another single frame's own label.
22	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
23	const WIDTH_TABLET = '80%';
24	// The original width set when this drawer shell was first built (2026-08-27) — matches Figma's
25	// "Desktop Small" exactly. Used by every viewport-independent narrow utility drawer (Find in
26	// Boutique today; Notify Me/Wishlist/Regional Storefront/Cookies/Login once those exist).
27	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';
28	// SFCC-11 (Cart build): the "X-Large — 82%" library annotation two paragraphs up is the
29	// named-size *system* value, not a measurement of the actual Cart composition. Re-measured the
30	// real frames directly (node 9323:65888 at 1920px, node 9323:65895 at 1440px, file
31	// QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs) — the cart panel itself (frame "pdp/drawer") is a FIXED 1186px at
32	// both widths; the backdrop gap grows instead of the panel. 82% of 1920 is 1574px — 388px
33	// wider than designed. This is the same annotation-vs-measurement trap the comment above
34	// already records once for Tablet; it recurred here for X-Large. 74.125rem = 1186px.
35	// Widths/min-widths/max-widths across drawer sizes are a live, unsettled area as of
36	// 2026-09-17 (Marcel) — this ships to the current measured Figma spec and may be
37	// reconciled once that broader call is made; not a final word on the sizing model.
38	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed fixed width with no --zimm-scale equivalent at this value.
39	const WIDTH_XLARGE = '74.125rem'; // 1186px
40	
41	// PDP drawer leaves a strip of backdrop visible below the panel on mobile (SFCC-736 AC 9,
42	// PO-approved 2026-08-21 — "so a user can easily navigate out"). Re-measured against node
43	// 40002218:42903 (SFCC-898): overlay 956px tall, panel 898px tall — exactly 58px. Only the
44	// `mobileGap` variant opts into this; the baseStyle defaults to full-height so utility
45	// drawers (wishlist auth, etc.) don't need to explicitly override it. No named spacing scale
46	// step lands on 58px — provisional raw value pending a foundation token.
47	const MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP = '3.625rem'; // 58px
48	
49	// Close-button inset, measured from the pdp/drawer header frames. `tablet`/`small`/`xLarge`/
50	// `mobile` all share the same measured inset (32px/40px) at every width — only `large` switches
51	// to the wider 48px/64px inset, at/above the tablet breakpoint. Below that breakpoint `large`'s
52	// own override doesn't apply either, and the baseStyle inset is used instead, which is also how
53	// the whole drawer collapses to the mobile treatment on a narrow viewport regardless of `size`.
54	const INSET_COMPACT = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)' };
55	const INSET_LARGE = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)' };
56	
57	// Header constants — from Figma drawer/header frame measurements.
58	// Compact horizontal inset (small/mobile): px=32px. Large desktop: px=64px.
59	// Small desktop header uses py=24px. Large desktop: container height=120px (row centred).
60	// Mobile base: container height=72px.
61	const HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'; // 32px
62	const HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)'; // 64px
63	const HEADER_PADDING_Y = 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'; // 24px — small desktop py
64	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed container heights with no --zimm-scale equivalents at these values.
65	const HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE = '120px';
66	const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '72px';
67	
68	export const ZimmDrawer = {
69	  parts: ['overlay', 'content', 'closeButton', 'header', 'headerTitle'],
70	  baseStyle: {
71	    // Explicit position/inset rather than relying on Chakra's own built-in `Drawer` overlay
72	    // styling — confirmed via inspection that it doesn't apply (renders `position: static`,
73	    // zero size) when the `<Drawer>` isn't given Chakra's own `size` prop, which this component
74	    // deliberately omits (see maxWidth note below). Owning it here avoids depending on that.
75	    overlay: {
76	      position: 'fixed',
77	      inset: 0,
78	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)',
79	      zIndex: 'overlay',
80	    },
81	    content: {
82	      // Chakra's own <DrawerContent> baked in a default white background
83	      // (@chakra-ui/theme's modal.js `baseStyleDialog`: `bg: colors.white`) that this recipe
84	      // never needed to set itself while that component was still in use — now that
85	      // ZimmDrawer hand-rolls its own content element (see index.tsx's file-level comment),
86	      // nothing supplies one unless it's set here. Matches Figma's pdp/drawer panel background
87	      // (bg-[var(--brand/color/palette/white,white)]) — --zimm-color-bg-07 resolves to the
88	      // same grey.white value (SFCC-898 — the panel briefly had no background at all).
89	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-07)',
90	      width: '100%',
91	      // Matches `width` at every step below — Chakra's own `Drawer` theme defaults to
92	      // `size="xs"` (maxW 20rem) when no `size` prop is passed to `<Drawer>` (deliberate: its
93	      // fixed size scale has no 50%/25% steps), and that default `maxW` otherwise still caps
94	      // our own `width` override since we never reset it.
95	      maxWidth: '100%',
96	      // A `height` reduction, not a `bottom` offset — Chakra's own Slide transition (see
97	      // @chakra-ui/transition's slide.js `placement: 'right'` case) pins the sliding wrapper
98	      // with `position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0`, a definite height. `bottom` on
99	      // this `position: relative` DrawerContent just shifts the box within that instead of
100	      // reliably opening a gap (SFCC-898 — mobile bottom gap wasn't rendering at all); a
101	      // percentage `height` resolves cleanly against that definite-height ancestor instead.
102	      // CodeRabbit (PR review): baseStyle should default to full-height so utility drawers
103	      // don't inherit the PDP-specific 58px backdrop strip — moved to the `mobile` variant.
104	      height: '100%',
105	      // Header stays fixed; only the content area (ZimmPdpDrawer's own `content` part) scrolls —
106	      // AC 10, "content area scrolls independently without the tab header scrolling".
107	      display: 'flex',
108	      flexDirection: 'column',
109	      overflow: 'hidden',
110	    },
111	    // Was missing `position: absolute` since this component's original commit — the
112	    // top/right insets below were silently no-ops (closeButton rendered as a normal in-flow
113	    // block instead of overlaying the header's corner), which is the root cause of SFCC-898's
114	    // close-button-misaligned-with-tabs defect across every breakpoint.
115	    //
116	    // height/display/alignItems/justifyContent: matches zimmTabs.css.ts's `menu.minHeight`
117	    // (DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT, zimmDrawerShared.ts) and centers the icon inside it — the
118	    // close icon's own intrinsic size doesn't equal the tab row's real rendered height, so
119	    // matching only `top` between the two (as before) left their vertical centers slightly
120	    // offset (SFCC-898, mobile). Only applies to the floating close button (no `title` passed) —
121	    // the inline title-row close button below is a normal flex child, not absolutely positioned.
122	    closeButton: {
123	      position: 'absolute',
124	      ...INSET_COMPACT,
125	      height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
126	      display: 'flex',
127	      alignItems: 'center',
128	      justifyContent: 'center',
129	    },
130	    // Drawer header — title (flex-1, left) + close button (right).
131	    // baseStyle applies the mobile/compact treatment: px=32px, container h=72px centred.
132	    // SFCC-926 (Figma): paddingBlock is 0 at mobile so the 72px minHeight controls the height
133	    // (flex centering handles vertical alignment). At md+ 24px block padding applies — matching
134	    // Figma's "small desktop py" spec without overriding the mobile 72px container height.
135	    header: {
136	      display: 'flex',
137	      alignItems: 'center',
138	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
139	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
140	      paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X,
141	      paddingBlock: 0,
142	      minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
143	      flexShrink: 0,
144	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
145	        paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
146	      },
147	    },
148	    headerTitle: {
149	      display: 'flex',
150	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
151	      alignItems: 'center',
152	      flex: '1 0 0',
153	      minWidth: 0,
154	      overflow: 'hidden',
155	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
156	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
157	    },
158	  },
159	  variants: {
160	    large: {
161	      content: {
162	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
163	          width: WIDTH_LARGE,
164	          maxWidth: WIDTH_LARGE,
165	          height: '100%',
166	        },
167	      },
168	      closeButton: {
169	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: INSET_LARGE,
170	      },
171	      header: {
172	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
173	          paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X,
174	          minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE,
175	        },
176	      },
177	    },
178	    // Figma's "Tablet" size — the tablet-range step for Product Details/Filters, which
179	    // graduates to `large` (Desktop Large) at the desktop breakpoint via the caller's own
180	    // useBreakpointValue (ZimmPdpDrawer never selects this variant itself).
181	    tablet: {
182	      content: {
183	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
184	          width: WIDTH_TABLET,
185	          maxWidth: WIDTH_TABLET,
186	          height: '100%',
187	        },
188	      },
189	    },
190	    // Figma's "Desktop Small" — always narrow, at every width above the mobile collapse. No
191	    // js-level graduation to another variant the way `tablet` graduates to `large` — this is
192	    // the whole point for its utility-drawer consumers (Find in Boutique today).
193	    small: {
194	      content: {
195	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
196	          width: WIDTH_SMALL,
197	          maxWidth: WIDTH_SMALL,
198	          height: '100%',
199	        },
200	      },
201	    },
202	    // Figma's "X-Large" (Cart) — not consumed anywhere yet (Cart is a full page today, not a
203	    // drawer), but the real value is already here under the right name for when that changes.
204	    // `maxWidth: '100%'` (not WIDTH_XLARGE) so a viewport narrower than 1186px but still ≥ `md`
205	    // doesn't overflow.
206	    xLarge: {
207	      content: {
208	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
209	          width: WIDTH_XLARGE,
210	          maxWidth: '100%',
211	          height: '100%',
212	        },
213	      },
214	      header: {
215	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
216	          minHeight: 'unset',
217	          paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
218	        },
219	      },
220	    },
221	    // CodeRabbit (PR review): 58px backdrop strip is PDP-specific (SFCC-736 AC 9, PO-approved)
222	    // and must not apply to utility drawers — scoped here to the explicit `mobile` variant.
223	    // Figma's "Mobile" size — only drawers that need the strip opt in; utility drawers
224	    // (wishlist auth, etc.) use `large` instead, which collapses to full-height via baseStyle.
225	    mobile: {
226	      content: {
227	        height: `calc(100% - ${MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP})`,
228	      },
229	    },
230	  },
231	};

> **Draft squad split — scope can still change as sprints are confirmed.**

Squad A owns this code. If you are from Squad B and need to touch these files, message the Squad A Lead directly before proceeding.

## Squad A Territory

```text
overrides/app/pages/home/
overrides/app/pages/product-detail/
overrides/app/pages/product-list/
overrides/app/pages/product-list/partials/
overrides/app/pages/cart/
overrides/app/pages/checkout/
overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/
overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/
overrides/app/pages/confirmation/
overrides/app/components/header/
overrides/app/components/footer/
overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/
overrides/app/components/list-menu/
overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express/
overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons/
overrides/app/components/multiship/
overrides/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/
overrides/app/hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multiship.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-pickup-shipment.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.ts
```

Note: `use-current-basket.ts` is listed here for reference but is **Tier 1** — do not modify it without Integration lead approval. `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, and `list-menu/` are **Tier 2** — coordinate with Squad B before touching.

## Scoping Rules for Squad A

- Do not modify `order-summary/` without notifying Squad B — it is Tier 2.
- Do not modify `use-current-basket.ts` — Tier 1, Integration lead owns it.
- Always scope to the specific partial — do not refactor the parent checkout page unless explicitly asked.
- Changes to express payment components require Integration lead awareness.
- `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — notify Squad B before any change.

## Good vs Bad Prompts (Squad A)

**Fixing a spacing issue in the shipping address form:**
✅ `In overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/shipping-address.tsx only, adjust the Stack spacing prop from 6 to 3 at the base breakpoint. Do not modify any theme files, hooks, or other partials.`
❌ `Fix the spacing in the checkout form` — Claude may touch multiple partials and theme tokens.

**Adding a gift message field:**
✅ `In overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/shipping-address.tsx only, add a gift message textarea below the address form using the existing React Hook Form field wrapper. Do not modify any hooks or order-summary.`
❌ `Add a gift message to checkout` — Claude may modify basket hooks and order summary.

7	
8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/index.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step — TypeScript annotations, the import path
12	 * rewrites documented below, and a temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live
13	 * against three real surfaces per the plan's copy-first stop, then removed) were the only
14	 * changes; styling/behaviour changes are this commit (plan step 2.2, see below), not that one.
15	 *
16	 * Import path rewrites, per .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an already-overridden
17	 * component from a new component":
18	 * - `item-variant` / `item-variant/item-image` / `item-variant/item-name` /
19	 *   `item-variant/item-attributes` / `item-variant/item-price`: this repo overrides all five
20	 *   (SFCC-270, this same commit), so these are relative imports rather than the base
21	 *   `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path — a base-path import here would silently exercise the
22	 *   unstyled base components in Storybook/Vitest instead of these overrides.
23	 * - `./bonus-product-quantity` / `./product-quantity-picker`: same reasoning, both overridden in
24	 *   this same commit, in this same folder.
25	 * - `responsive` (`HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`): also already overridden in this repo
26	 *   (overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx) — and not just a styling port, a genuine
27	 *   behavioural difference (it moves the mobile/desktop split to Chakra's `md` breakpoint instead
28	 *   of the base's `lg`) — so this is rewritten to a relative import too, for the same reason.
29	 * - `shared/ui`, `loading-spinner`, `utils/utils`, and the `app/hooks` barrel (`useCurrency`/
30	 *   `useDerivedProduct`) are NOT overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing
31	 *   at time of writing) — these stay on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path, since
32	 *   there is no local override to redirect to.
33	 *
34	 * `SfccProduct` is kept as `any` with a named alias rather than a structural type invented from
35	 * usage — this package ships no TypeScript types for this shape, matching the same documented gap
36	 * at overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:136-151.
37	 *
38	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec via product-item.css.ts's
39	 * `ZimmCartItem` recipe (`row`/`details`/`info` parts, applied through `sx` — see that recipe's
40	 * own docblock for why `sx`, not `__css`, is required on a plain Flex/Stack here). The image's
41	 * own default width moved out of this file entirely — item-image.tsx now supplies its own
42	 * responsive default via item-variant.css.ts's `image` part, so the `mr`-based gap this file
43	 * used to add is replaced by the `row` part's own Figma-specified `gap`.
44	 * `CartItemVariantAttributes` now also renders with `combineAttributeValues`, per the Figma
45	 * spec's single "colour, size" string (see that component's own file). The two `display={[...]}`
46	 * responsive-array primaryAction visibility toggles are replaced with this file's own already-
47	 * imported `HideOnMobile`/`HideOnDesktop` (both already used here for `deliveryActions`) — the
48	 * original arrays split at Chakra's default `sm` (480px), one breakpoint earlier than this
49	 * file's own `md` (768px) split everywhere else; no Figma value distinguishes this, so it is
50	 * unified to the same `md` split as the rest of this file rather than preserved as a second,
51	 * unexplained breakpoint — flagged in this build's report as a disclosed interpretation, not a
52	 * tested requirement.
53	 *
54	 * Gift-card *detection* is still NOT implemented — unchanged finding from the prior round: no
55	 * real signal for "this line item is a digital gift card" exists anywhere in this codebase or
56	 * the commerce SDK types at time of writing (`GiftCertificateItem` exists in the SDK but is a
57	 * structurally different, wholly separate basket line-item shape that this component's own
58	 * render tree — `useDerivedProduct`, `ItemVariantProvider`'s `SfccProduct` shape — is not built
59	 * to receive at all). That finding stands as-is; it was independently confirmed by two separate
60	 * reviewers in the prior round and is not re-litigated here.
61	 *
62	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework: the *capability* half is now built. `hideStepperAndActions` (optional,
63	 * defaults falsy so every existing caller is unaffected) suppresses the quantity stepper
64	 * (BonusProductQuantity/ProductQuantityPicker) and every actions surface (primaryAction,
65	 * secondaryActions, deliveryActions) when true, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2's gift-card
66	 * variant note ("no stepper, no actions ... build ZimmCartItem with the stepper and actions row
67	 * optional"). Nothing else in this component's render tree branches on it — the 5-field
68	 * label/value block that same note describes for a real gift-card line item is not built here,
69	 * and remains for whichever future commit ends up owning real gift-card detection.
70	 *
71	 * SFCC-795 (plan step 3.2): `message` (optional, prop-driven) renders a ZimmInlineMessage between
72	 * the quantity stepper and the actions row, per .claude/session-notes.md §11.2 ("inline message
73	 * (error/warning) sits between the stepper and the actions"). This component does not itself
74	 * determine OOS/partial-OOS/unavailable/max-quantity state — OOS/partial-OOS detection is
75	 * SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's, both later-sprint tickets. Undefined (every
76	 * existing caller today) renders nothing and leaves the Item Details gap at its existing 12px
77	 * desktop value (`ZimmCartItem`'s `hasError` resolution prop, product-item.css.ts, derived below
78	 * from `message?.variant === 'error'`).
79	 */
80	import React from 'react';
81	
82	// Chakra Components
83	import {
84	  Box,
85	  Fade,
86	  Flex,
87	  Stack,
88	  Text,
89	  useMultiStyleConfig,
90	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
91	
92	// Project Components
93	import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '../responsive';
94	import ItemVariantProvider from '../item-variant';
95	import CartItemVariantImage from '../item-variant/item-image';
96	import CartItemVariantName from '../item-variant/item-name';
97	import CartItemVariantAttributes from '../item-variant/item-attributes';
98	import CartItemVariantPrice from '../item-variant/item-price';
99	import LoadingSpinner from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/loading-spinner';
100	import BonusProductQuantity from './bonus-product-quantity';
101	import ProductQuantityPicker from './product-quantity-picker';
102	import { ZimmInlineMessage } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage';
103	
104	// Hooks
105	import { useCurrency, useDerivedProduct } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks';
106	
107	const ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartItem';
108	
109	type SfccProduct = any;
110	
111	type ProductItemProps = {
112	  product: SfccProduct;
113	  primaryAction?: React.ReactNode;
114	  secondaryActions?: React.ReactNode;
115	  deliveryActions?: React.ReactNode;
116	  onItemQuantityChange?: (quantity: number) => any;
117	  /**
118	   * Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render
119	   * body — kept here only to mirror that declared surface one-for-one (zero functional diff,
120	   * SFCC-270). No return-type guarantee to derive from PropTypes.func, so typed loosely.
121	   */
122	  onAddItemToCart?: (...args: any[]) => any;
123	  showLoading?: boolean;
124	  /** Declared on the base file's propTypes but never read inside this component's own render body — see onAddItemToCart above. */
125	  isWishlistItem?: boolean;
126	  containerStyles?: Record<string, any>;
127	  isRemoving?: boolean;
128	  pickupInStore?: boolean;
129	  /**
130	   * Gift-card capability slot (SFCC-270 round 2 rework, session-notes.md §11.2): when true,
131	   * suppresses the quantity stepper and every actions surface (primaryAction, secondaryActions,
132	   * deliveryActions). Defaults falsy so every existing caller's rendering is unchanged. This
133	   * component does not itself detect a gift-card line item — see this file's own docblock — a
134	   * caller sets this explicitly once real detection exists.
135	   */
136	  hideStepperAndActions?: boolean;
137	  /**
138	   * Cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2), rendered via
139	   * ZimmInlineMessage between the quantity stepper and the actions row. Presentation only — see
140	   * ZimmInlineMessage's own docblock: this component does not itself determine OOS/partial-OOS/
141	   * unavailable/max-quantity state, a caller passes the already-resolved variant + copy.
142	   * Undefined (the default for every existing caller) renders nothing and leaves the Item
143	   * Details gap at its existing 12px desktop value.
144	   */
145	  message?: {
146	    variant: 'error' | 'warning';
147	    text: string;
148	  };
149	};
150	
151	/**
152	 * Component representing a product item usually in a list with details about the product - name, variant, pricing, etc.
153	 * @param {Object} product Product to be represented in the list item.
154	 * @param {node} primaryAction Child component representing the most prominent action to be performed by the user.
155	 * @param {node} secondaryActions Child component representing the other actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
156	 * @param {node} deliveryActions Child component representing the delivery actions relevant to the product to be performed by the user.
157	 * @param {func} onItemQuantityChange callback function to be invoked whenever item quantity changes.
158	 * @param {boolean} showLoading Renders a loading spinner with overlay if set to true.
159	 * @returns A JSX element representing product item in a list (eg: wishlist, cart, etc).
160	 */
161	const ProductItem = ({
162	  product,
163	  primaryAction,
164	  secondaryActions,
165	  deliveryActions,
166	  // CodeRabbit (SFCC-11 cumulative review): default was `noop`, a synchronous no-op returning
167	  // `undefined` - but product-quantity-picker.tsx's handleQuantityChange unconditionally calls
168	  // `.then(...)` on this callback's return value. A caller that omits this optional prop and
169	  // then changes quantity would throw. This default resolves to `true` (a valid change) so the
170	  // `.then` chain completes normally instead.
171	  onItemQuantityChange = async () => true,
172	  showLoading = false,
173	  containerStyles = {},
174	  isRemoving = false,
175	  pickupInStore = false,
176	  hideStepperAndActions = false,
177	  message,
178	}: ProductItemProps) => {
179	  const { stepQuantity, showInventoryMessage, inventoryMessage, quantity, setQuantity } = useDerivedProduct(
180	    product,
181	    false,
182	    false,
183	    pickupInStore,
184	  );
185	  const { currency: activeCurrency } = useCurrency();
186	  // hasError drives ZimmCartItem's own Item Details gap widening (12px -> 16px desktop) — see
187	  // product-item.css.ts's docblock — derived from `message`, not a separate prop, so the two can
188	  // never disagree about whether an error-variant message is currently showing.
189	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_RECIPE, { hasError: message?.variant === 'error' });
190	  return (
191	    <Box position="relative" data-testid={`sf-cart-item-${product.productId ? product.productId : product.id}`}>
192	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
193	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
194	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
195	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
196	            <CartItemVariantImage />
197	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
198	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
199	                <Stack spacing={1}>
200	                  <CartItemVariantName />
201	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
202	                  <HideOnDesktop>
203	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
204	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
205	                    </Box>
206	                  </HideOnDesktop>
207	                </Stack>
208	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
209	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
210	                )}
211	              </Flex>
212	
213	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
214	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
215	              )}
216	
217	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
218	                <Stack spacing={1}>
219	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
220	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
221	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
222	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
223	                    ) : (
224	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
225	                        product={product}
226	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
227	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
228	                        quantity={quantity}
229	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
230	                      />
231	                    ))}
232	                </Stack>
233	                <Stack>
234	                  <HideOnMobile>
235	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
236	                  </HideOnMobile>
237	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
238	                </Stack>
239	              </Flex>
240	
241	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
242	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
243	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
244	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
245	
246	              <Box>
247	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
248	                  <Fade in={true}>
249	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
250	                      {inventoryMessage}
251	                    </Text>
252	                  </Fade>
253	                )}
254	              </Box>
255	
256	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
257	            </Stack>
258	          </Flex>
259	
260	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
261	            <HideOnDesktop>
262	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
263	            </HideOnDesktop>
264	          )}
265	        </Stack>
266	      </ItemVariantProvider>
267	    </Box>
268	  );
269	};
270	
271	export default ProductItem;
272

1	// Icon sizes — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026 (Handover tokens.md § Icon Sizes)
2	//
3	// Deliberately NOT registered as `theme.sizes`. Chakra's `sizes.lg` is 32rem and
4	// backs every `w`/`h`/`boxSize` token across the base retail-react-app, so
5	// remapping these names would resize base components. Import these constants
6	// directly instead — the same pattern component overrides already use for
7	// FONT_MEDIUM: `<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />`.
8	export const iconSizes = {
9	  xl: '24px',
10	  lg: '20px',
11	  md: '16px',
12	  sm: '12px',
13	} as const;
14	
15	// Action (button) sizing — source: Handover tokens/spacing.css (--zimm-size-action-*).
16	// The CSS-var twins already exist in zimmTokens.ts. zimmButton.css.ts (the single source
17	// of truth for actual button styling) uses var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg/md) directly,
18	// which resolves to these Figma-confirmed values (52px / 40px).
19	export const actionSizes = {
20	  height: {
21	    lg: '52px',
22	    md: '40px',
23	  },
24	  paddingX: {
25	    lg: '32px',
26	    md: '20px',
27	  },
28	  gap: '16px',
29	} as const;
30	
31	// Mega-menu sizing — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026, Figma node 40002429:7215
32	// (two-column "Expanded Menu" Nav Group, confirmed against SFCC-883).
33	export const megaMenuSizes = {
34	  twoColumnMaxWidth: '700px',
35	} as const;

1	/**
2	 * SFCC-270 round 2 rework, extended post-rework (found live in Storybook by Marcel, not by this
3	 * suite). Proves three stacked bugs are actually fixed TOGETHER, not just that the symbols were
4	 * added:
5	 *   1. `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` (base SFCC hook, unconditional
6	 *      `product.variants.filter(...)`) needs `variants` to be an array on the mock product.
7	 *   2. `useDerivedProduct` unconditionally calls `useSelectedStore()`, which throws without a
8	 *      real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
9	 *   3. `item-attributes.tsx`'s `useCurrentBasket()` call has its own separate transitive chain
10	 *      (`useSFPayments` -> `useAppOrigin` -> `useOrigin`) that calls the SDK's
11	 *      `useServerContext()` and destructures `res` from it unconditionally, before `useOrigin`'s
12	 *      own `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branch (which never touches `res`) is reached. This
13	 *      file previously mocked `useCurrentBasket` away entirely, which hid this bug completely —
14	 *      unmocked now so this suite actually exercises the real chain. `ServerContext.Provider`
15	 *      with `value={{}}` matches exactly what the real app's own browser bootstrap supplies
16	 *      client-side (`ssr/browser/main.js`'s `OuterApp`) — confirmed by reading that file.
17	 *
18	 * Deliberately does NOT use index.test.tsx's harness — that file mocks the whole
19	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks` barrel's `useDerivedProduct`, which would hide both
20	 * bugs this file exists to catch. This renders through the real, unmocked `useDerivedProduct` ->
21	 * `useVariationAttributes` -> `isVariantValueOrderable` / `useSelectedStore` chain, with a real
22	 * `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor.
23	 *
24	 * `useMultiSite` and `useCurrency` are still mocked, for a reason that has nothing to do with
25	 * this build's own logic: `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts` (the barrel both
26	 * `MultiSiteProvider`/`CurrencyProvider` and `use-multi-site.js`/`use-currency.js` resolve
27	 * through) is a `.js` file containing inline JSX, which Vite's transform cannot parse as a
28	 * plain `.js` file — confirmed empirically (this file's first draft imported `MultiSiteProvider`
29	 * from that barrel directly and vitest failed at import-analysis on
30	 * `app/contexts/index.js:49`, not at any assertion). This is the same parse failure
31	 * item-variant/index.test.tsx's own docblock already documents and works around by mocking
32	 * `use-multi-site` instead of using a real `MultiSiteProvider`; extended here to `useCurrency`
33	 * for the same reason. `StoreLocatorProvider` itself is real: `use-selected-store.js` and
34	 * `store-locator-provider.jsx` both import `StoreLocatorContext` via that file's own direct path
35	 * (`.../app/contexts/store-locator-provider`), never through the barrel, so it never hits this
36	 * parse wall — confirmed by reading both files' imports, not assumed.
37	 *
38	 * Two more pragmatic mocks, both explained inline at their own `vi.mock`/`beforeEach`: `useStores`
39	 * (an unrelated dual-module-instance QueryClient issue, not this build's own code) and a
40	 * `window.matchMedia` polyfill (jsdom has none; item-price.tsx's `useBreakpointValue` needs it —
41	 * the same pre-existing gap and fix product-item/index.test.tsx's own `beforeEach` already uses).
42	 * Neither affects what this file actually proves: that a real `StoreLocatorProvider` ancestor and
43	 * an array-valued `variants` together stop the render from throwing.
44	 */
45	import React from 'react';
46	import { describe, test, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
47	import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react';
48	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';
49	import { IntlProvider } from 'react-intl';
50	import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
51	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
52	import { CommerceApiProvider } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
53	import { StoreLocatorProvider } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/contexts/store-locator-provider';
54	import { ServerContext } from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/contexts';
55	import theme from 'app/theme';
56	import ProductItem from '.';
57	
58	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site', () => ({
59	  default: vi.fn(() => ({ site: { id: 'ZimmermannAU' }, buildUrl: (path: string) => path })),
60	}));
61	
62	// Cannot use this factory's `importOriginal` here: it resolves the barrel itself
63	// (`app/hooks/index.js`), which re-exports `useCurrency` from `use-currency.js`, which imports
64	// `CurrencyContext` from the broken `app/contexts` barrel — so `importOriginal()` transitively
65	// hits the same parse wall as importing `MultiSiteProvider` does (confirmed empirically: this
66	// was the first thing tried here, and it failed at the identical `app/contexts/index.js:49`
67	// parse error). `vi.importActual` on `use-derived-product`'s own direct sub-path sidesteps it —
68	// that file's own dependency chain never touches `app/contexts` (confirmed by grepping it and
69	// every hook it imports).
70	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks', async () => {
71	  const { useDerivedProduct } = await vi.importActual<
72	    typeof import('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product')
73	  >('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product');
74	  return {
75	    useCurrency: () => ({ currency: 'AUD', setCurrency: vi.fn() }),
76	    useDerivedProduct,
77	  };
78	});
79	
80	// Same fix as product-item/index.test.tsx's own: PromoPopover imports the base SFCC icons
81	// barrel, which has a top-level side effect that throws under Vitest (testing.md's documented
82	// ZimmIcon gap, same root cause via a different import path).
83	vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-popover', () => ({
84	  default: ({ children }: { children?: React.ReactNode }) => <>{children}</>,
85	}));
86	
87	// `useStores` is mocked too (in addition to usePromotions/useProducts/useProduct, needed for the
88	// same reason as product-item/index.test.tsx's own): the REAL `useSelectedStore` (unmocked, the
89	// actual thing this file proves doesn't throw) calls it internally, and the real `useStores` hit
90	// an unrelated environment issue here — `@tanstack/react-query`'s `useQueryClient()` not finding
91	// this file's own `QueryClientProvider` (a dual-module-instance style mismatch, not anything this
92	// build's own code controls). Mocking only `useStores` still exercises `useSelectedStore`'s own
93	// real body — including the `useContext(StoreLocatorContext)` throw-if-missing check this file
94	// exists to prove no longer throws — while sidestepping that unrelated plumbing issue.
95	vi.mock('@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react', async (importOriginal) => {
96	  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import('@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react')>();
97	  return {
98	    ...actual,
99	    usePromotions: () => ({ data: undefined }),
100	    useProducts: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
101	    useProduct: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
102	    useStores: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
103	    // Same dual-module-instance QueryClient issue as useStores above, surfacing here now that
104	    // useCurrentBasket (unmocked, see this file's own docblock) calls this for real internally.
105	    useCustomerBaskets: () => ({ data: undefined, isLoading: false }),
106	  };
107	});
108	
109	const storyQueryClient = new QueryClient({
110	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
111	});
112	
113	// `useStores` (called for real inside the real `useSelectedStore`, unmocked above) is left real
114	// too — it resolves with `enabled: false` (no selectedStoreId in this jsdom's empty
115	// localStorage), so it registers a disabled query and never actually fetches, matching
116	// index.stories.tsx's own documented reasoning for its inert CommerceApiProvider/proxy setup.
117	const renderWithStoryProviders = (ui: React.ReactElement) =>
118	  render(
119	    <ServerContext.Provider value={{}}>
120	      <ChakraProvider theme={theme}>
121	        <MemoryRouter>
122	          <QueryClientProvider client={storyQueryClient}>
123	            <CommerceApiProvider
124	              clientId="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
125	              organizationId="f_ecom_storybook_001"
126	              shortCode="storybook"
127	              siteId="ZimmermannAU"
128	              locale="en-AU"
129	              currency="AUD"
130	              proxy="https://storybook.invalid/mobify/proxy/api"
131	              redirectURI="https://storybook.invalid/callback"
132	              disableAuthInit
133	              silenceWarnings
134	            >
135	              <StoreLocatorProvider config={{ defaultCountryCode: 'AU', defaultPostalCode: '2000' }}>
136	                <IntlProvider locale="en-AU" defaultLocale="en-AU">
137	                  {ui}
138	                </IntlProvider>
139	              </StoreLocatorProvider>
140	            </CommerceApiProvider>
141	          </QueryClientProvider>
142	        </MemoryRouter>
143	      </ChakraProvider>
144	    </ServerContext.Provider>,
145	  );
146	
147	// Mirrors index.stories.tsx's own MOCK_LINE_ITEM shape, including the round 2 `variants: []` fix.
148	const MOCK_LINE_ITEM = {
149	  itemId: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a1b2c3d4e5f6',
150	  productId: '25595021M',
151	  id: '25595021M',
152	  productName: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
153	  name: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress',
154	  price: 495,
155	  priceAfterItemDiscount: 495,
156	  pricePerUnit: 495,
157	  quantity: 1,
158	  stepQuantity: 1,
159	  minOrderQuantity: 1,
160	  imageGroups: [
161	    {
162	      viewType: 'small',
163	      images: [{ alt: 'Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress', link: 'https://example.invalid/lilac-sand.jpg' }],
164	    },
165	  ],
166	  variationAttributes: [
167	    { id: 'color', name: 'Colour', values: [{ value: 'JJ5FUXX', name: 'Lilac Sand', orderable: true }] },
168	    { id: 'size', name: 'Size', values: [{ value: 'ONESIZE', name: 'One Size', orderable: true }] },
169	  ],
170	  variationValues: { color: 'JJ5FUXX', size: 'ONESIZE' },
171	  variants: [],
172	};
173	
174	describe('ProductItem — Storybook story render (SFCC-270 round 2)', () => {
175	  // jsdom has no matchMedia implementation, and item-price.tsx's `isDesktop` uses
176	  // useBreakpointValue internally, which calls it — unrelated to either bug this file exists to
177	  // catch, same pre-existing gap and same per-file polyfill product-item/index.test.tsx's own
178	  // beforeEach already uses (not a change to the frozen vitest.setup.ts).
179	  beforeEach(() => {
180	    Object.defineProperty(window, 'matchMedia', {
181	      writable: true,
182	      value: vi.fn().mockImplementation((query: string) => ({
183	        matches: false,
184	        media: query,
185	        onchange: null,
186	        addListener: vi.fn(),
187	        removeListener: vi.fn(),
188	        addEventListener: vi.fn(),
189	        removeEventListener: vi.fn(),
190	        dispatchEvent: vi.fn(),
191	      })),
192	    });
193	  });
194	
195	  test('Default-equivalent: renders through the real, unmocked useDerivedProduct/useSelectedStore chain without throwing', () => {
196	    expect(() =>
197	      renderWithStoryProviders(

199	      ),

201	
202	    expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 2 })).toHaveTextContent('Lilac Sand Silk Midi Dress');
203	  });

content.text: Found it — my docblock at `index.tsx:34` cites another file's literal `styles.value` JSX attribute inside a `/** */` block comment. `recipeParts.test.ts`'s `stripLineComments` only strips `//` comments, so this citation is misread as a real part-read. This is my bug to fix (not the guard's) — I'll reword the citation to avoid the literal pattern.

 * so a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.

Fix is in the 9 files below (branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart`, confirmed not `develop`/`main` before starting). **Files touched, by what changed:** 1. `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx` — added `InfoSolidIcon` (circle + two line segments, viewBox 0 0 16 16, both shapes `stroke="currentColor" fill="none"`), inserted directly after `InfoSelectedIcon`'s closing `});`, with a citation comment (Figma node `I9323:106685;40002929:8789`, the 3-instance confirmation, why no scaling correction, why the two strokes stay separate segments, and the `#969696`-coincidence note per your brief). 2. `overrides/app/components/icons/index.tsx` — **no change**, confirmed: `export * from './zimm'` (line 8) already carries `InfoSolidIcon` through, no explicit re-export conflicts with it. 3. `overrides/app/components/icons/icons.stories.tsx` — added `InfoSolidIcon` to the import block and both catalog arrays, at the specified alphabetical spots. 4. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx` — added `'info-solid'` to `ZimmIconType` (between `'info-selected'`/`'location'`), the import, and `ICON_MAP`. Judgement call (flagged, not pre-specified): added a short comment on the type union and `ICON_MAP` entry, parallel to the existing footer-specific-icon comment, noting `info-solid` isn't part of the "34 of 34" Figma-1892:59595 count — same reasoning your brief already asked for in the sibling stories file, extended here for consistency; didn't touch the "34 of 34" line itself since that count is still accurate. 5. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.stories.tsx` — added `CART_TYPES = ['info-solid']` beside `FOOTER_TYPES`, with an equivalent provenance comment, and a matching "Cart-specific (pending Figma spec)" grid section in the `AllTypes` story. `FIGMA_TYPES` untouched. 6. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/zimmInlineMessage.css.ts` — rewritten from single-node `defineStyleConfig` to `{parts: ['root','text'], baseStyle, variants}`, following `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s plain-object precedent exactly. `root` = flex row (`alignItems: 'flex-start'`, `gap: var(--zimm-scale-xs)`, `width: 'full'`); `text` = the old `baseStyle` (`textStyle: 'caption'`, `fontWeight` regular override) plus `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` so the message wraps against the icon instead of overflowing. No `icon` part — documented why (`ZimmIcon`'s `color` prop defaults to `currentColor`, which Chakra's `Icon` passes straight through as inline CSS, so it inherits `root`'s colour for free — verified by reading `@chakra-ui/icon`'s actual source, not assumed). Docblock rewritten per your instruction, all prior citations (session-notes.md §11.2, the regular-weight-override reasoning, the no-low-stock-variant rule) preserved and re-pointed at the new part names. 7. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx` — `useStyleConfig` → `useMultiStyleConfig`, variable named `styles`, reads exactly `styles.root`/`styles.text`. Renders `{variant === 'warning' && }` before the text, inside a `` that now carries `aria-live`/`data-testid` (moved off the old single `

`, onto the new wrapping `div`, per your target shape). `size="md"` confirmed against `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` = 16px, matching Figma exactly. 8. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/zimmInlineMessage.css.test.ts` — all property paths updated to the nested shape (`.variants!.error.root.color`, `.baseStyle.text.textStyle`/`.fontWeight`, `.baseStyle.root.width`), same non-null-assertion comments kept, plus a new test asserting `parts` is exactly `['root', 'text']`. 9. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.test.tsx` — added the `ZimmIcon` mock (footerNavColumn/zimmSubscribeSection pattern, adapted to forward `type` via `data-type` since these assertions need it), plus two new tests: warning renders the mock icon with `data-type="info-solid"`, error never renders it. All 4 pre-existing tests kept, unchanged in intent. 10. `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.test.tsx` — added the identical `ZimmIcon` mock, and nothing else. Confirmed by inspection this was actually required: the file's existing `variant: 'warning'` test (line ~281, pre-existing, not written by me) would otherwise hit the now-real `ZimmIcon` render for the first time and throw under Vitest. Verified via a full-suite run before vs. after — this is the only file in that family that needed it (`index.stories.tsx`, `product-item.css.ts`, `product-item.css.test.ts` genuinely didn't, confirmed by reading them, not assumed). **A real bug I hit and fixed, not flagged, because it was mine:** my first draft of `zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx` quoted another file's `styles.value` JSX attribute verbatim inside a `/** */` docblock citation. `recipeParts.test.ts`'s comment-stripping only handles `//` lines, not `/* */` blocks, so its mechanical part-vs-read reconciliation misread that citation as a real usage and failed (`zimmInlineMessage` now being a multipart recipe for the first time is what newly exposed this — it never ran this check before). Reworded the citation to drop the literal `styles.value` substring; re-ran the guard clean. It renders `ProductItem` with no `message` prop at all in both its tests, so this isn't about the icon ever actually rendering — it's a module-evaluation-time crash, unavoidable in any unmocked consumer of `ProductItem` now that this rework exists. Your brief named `product-item/index.test.tsx` for exactly this class of fix but didn't mention this second, similarly-named file (easy to miss — `index.stories.test.tsx` isn't `index.stories.tsx`, which you did correctly mark out-of-scope). I confirmed by reading it that the identical one-line mock (`vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', ...)`) would fix it, and that it's the only other affected file in the repo (verified via a full-suite run, not sampling) — but I did not apply it, since it's outside every file this step named. That's the one thing between here and a fully green `npm run test`. **Judgement calls I made, flagged for your ratification:** - The `info-solid` provenance comments in `zimmIcon/index.tsx` (item 4 above) — not explicitly requested, added by direct analogy to the footer-icon precedent already in that same file, and to match what you did request in the sibling stories file. Easy to revert if you'd rather leave `ZimmIconType`/`ICON_MAP` uncommented there. - `text.flex: 1` / `text.minWidth: 0` in the recipe — you explicitly left this as "use your judgement." Chose the standard flex-child-text-wrapping pair; no Figma measurement backs the exact values (there's nothing to measure — it's a structural CSS reset, not a design value), so no token/citation applies. **What you're missing:** the `product-item/index.stories.test.tsx` gap above is the main one. Separately: this rework makes `ZimmIcon` reachable from `ProductItem`'s import graph for the first time — any *other* not-yet-written test that imports `ProductItem` (or `ZimmInlineMessage` directly) without the mock will hit this same crash going forward; worth a line in whatever onboarding note covers the existing "ZimmIcon throws under Vitest" gap, since the blast radius just grew from "components that render an icon" to "anything that imports this cart-item chain at all."
